create.name: Way of the Forest Empty Mountain Zen Hermitage
create.bio:
Forest Way Zen is a small Zen community based at a bush hermitage in Doonan, in the Sunshine Coast hinterland of Queensland. Its teacher, Reverend Doshin Kusan Rōshi, started the group in 1989. He trained for many years with Subhana Barzaghi Rōshi of the Diamond Sangha, spent an Ango training period with Robert Aitken Rōshi in Hawaii and was named a Rōshi in 2015; in 2020 James Ford Rōshi ordained him as a Sōtō Zen priest and gave him transmission. The hermitage now brings the two streams together, keeping Sōtō forms, chanting and just sitting (shikantaza) alongside the koan curriculum of the Diamond Sangha.

Members gather at the Doonan zendo on Wednesday evenings for sitting, chanting and a talk by the Rōshi, and there are online sittings on Tuesday and Thursday evenings and on Saturday mornings with chanting and a teisho. One-day zazenkai and short and longer sesshin are held through the year, and students can arrange to see the teacher on any day. Free introductory workshops on Zen history, posture and liturgy are offered from time to time, online or in person, and the website carries Kusan's essays, talks and sesshin poems.

courses.title: Weekly Zen meditation groups
courses.description: A Wednesday-evening sitting with chanting and a talk by the Rōshi at the Doonan zendo, plus online sittings on Tuesday and Thursday evenings and a Saturday-morning online session with chanting and teisho. The same page lists monthly zazenkai and sesshin; newcomers ring the teacher first.

courses.title: An Introduction to Zen Buddhism Workshop
courses.description: A workshop for complete beginners on the history and ideas of Zen, how to begin and sit comfortably, and the chanting and forms of this school, run by Rev. Doshin Kusan online or in person when there is enough interest.
courses.price: These workshops are offered for free

free_resources.title: Writings and articles by Rev. Doshin Kusan
free_resources.description: Essays, dharma talks and sesshin poems by the hermitage's teacher, on suffering and the Four Noble Truths, Sōtō liturgy such as the Five Remembrances, dependent arising and Zen practice in Australian life.
